analysis.title: The Point for Europe, Thursday, 05 November 2026
key_insights: Rheinmetall pre-released Q3 headline numbers and cut FY26 guidance to sales of EUR13.2bn (previously EUR13.7-14.2bn) and a margin of 18.5% (previously 19%). Citi cuts 2026 forecasts to match and trims later years by 2-3% on sales and 4-5% on profits, mainly in Weapons & Ammunition (W&A) and Naval. It views much of the 2026 miss as delayed, not lost. Target price falls to EUR1,374 from EUR1,408, Buy kept.

Citi values Rheinmetall's W&A division at about 6x 2028 EV/EBIT (about EUR306 per share) and the rest at about 20x (about EUR1,068 per share including net cash). It expects W&A to come down sharply once European stockpiles are replenished, which it says may take 5-10 years post-conflict.

Citi Quant data shows European Aerospace in the two-way debate quadrant, with long crowding up w/w but the sector still more bearish m/m. MTU and Melrose led the weekly improvement. Airbus and Safran stay highly crowded on both sides. Rolls-Royce stays in the investor apathy zone.

European Defense remains consensus long and became more bullish m/m on lower short positioning. Dassault and BAE improved w/w, Leonardo and Thales keep strong long positioning, Rheinmetall worsened but stays in consensus long. Renk is the only consensus short.

DNB holds its Capital Markets Day on 10 November. Citi expects emphasis on the Norwegian personal franchise (about 5 products per customer), Large Corporate growth outside Norway via DNB Carnegie, and cost initiatives around technology and AI. Possible targets include cost growth below 2%, a reiterated fee growth ambition above 9% and a return on equity ambition above 15%.

Nordea: Citi discusses its performance since the Buy The Dip note and the Danish AML investigation as a potential tail risk. The outcome is due 9 November, and Citi's model includes no fines beyond what Nordea has provisioned.

Arm reported F2Q27 with a 5% sales beat and 8% EPS beat on licensing strength and Cloud AI momentum, offsetting lower royalties from smartphone weakness. Data Center royalties doubled y/y, and management has more confidence in the Arm AGI CPU, with customer engagements, signed purchase orders and better supply visibility. Rated Buy.

Novo Nordisk 3Q was mixed. The adjusted sales and operating income guide points to roughly 3% FY26 consensus upgrades. Citi raised FY26 estimates 3-5% on Wegovy Pill sales but cut outer-year estimates by up to 6% on 2027 uncertainty and competition from 2028, notably Lilly's retatrutide. TP DKK298 from DKK296, Neutral/High Risk.

Ferrari delivered a 22% share of 'specials' in Q3, which Citi says was by design. It met Q3 earnings and EBIT margin expectations and guided FY26 EBIT up about 1%. Citi says consensus more than reflects roughly 30% EBIT margins and 8-10% EPS growth. At 36x P/E it stays Neutral, TP EUR375 from EUR347.

BMW is up after a profit warning, following a 37% YTD decline. China, pricing and raw materials remain headwinds into FY27. Possible positives are sales of the new NK BEV models and faster cost restructuring. Shares trade almost 20% below net industrial cash. Citi keeps a positive Catalyst Watch and a Neutral rating.

Leonardo: Sierra Nevada pulled out of the US Navy UJTS trainer program, leaving the Beechcraft/Leonardo M-345N as sole bidder, with award expected Q3 2027. Citi assumes a 50% Leonardo share of the roughly $10bn, 216-jet program at 10% margins, about EUR500m EBIT, worth about 1% of Leonardo's roughly EUR30bn market cap.

Aker BP: bp is exploring a sale of about 5% of the company, and Citi thinks a full exit is possible. With about 35% production growth 2026-28 already priced at about 20x EV/2P and two large shareholders potentially selling, Citi sees an overhang and no compelling entry point on a risk-adjusted basis.
Geberit expects sequential volume moderation into 4Q on tougher comparables and softer October momentum. Margins should hold on product mix, lower opex and price realization. TP unchanged, Neutral.
Wolters Kluwer stays a preferred pick after a trading update. Restructuring charges were guided higher while FY26E margin guidance was reiterated. Shares trade at 14.7x FY27E P/E.

Flutter: Citi cut FY26e revenue by 2% and adjusted EBITDA by 9%, and adjusted EPS by 23%, after 3Q26 missed its estimates and FY26 guidance was lowered, mostly on adverse sports results. FY27/28e EBITDA falls 4% each year, with larger FanDuel Predicts losses in the US and Brazil assumed closed through 1Q27. TP $90 from $91, Buy.

Evonik: at a break price of about EUR17, the share price implies about 65% deal probability for a BASF combination. Evonik management does not see the industrial logic of a BASF/Evonik deal, thinks an equity raise to fund an acquisition is unlikely, and says its order book is clearly stronger than a year ago.

Zalando: Citi raised FY26e/FY27e GMV forecasts by 0.4%/0.7% and revenue by 0.2%/0.5% after solid 3Q26. FY26e GMV growth is +5.6% and revenue +3.0%, at the lower end of guidance. Adjusted EBIT forecast is EUR712m against guidance of EUR680-720m. TP unchanged at EUR39.

Stora Enso: demand is mixed, with subdued European construction. Citi trims FY26e/27e EBIT slightly but expects significant EBIT and margin growth. The separation of Bergslagets Skogar should simplify the group. Buy, TP EUR12.

Schaeffler plans about 2,660 further job reductions, with up to EUR300m run-rate savings by 2030 and EUR480m one-time charges in FY26e. Citi cuts FY27-28e EPS by about 10%. FY26-28e adjusted EBIT is EUR1,057m/EUR1,333m/EUR1,689m. TP EUR11 from EUR12, Buy / High Risk.
Technogym upgraded to Buy from Neutral with a EUR17 TP (from EUR15). Citi sees Q3 organic growth of about +3% ex-FX as the trough.
Huhtamaki: Citi cuts FY27e EBIT by about 7% on a delayed North America margin recovery. FY26e EBIT is broadly unchanged. TP EUR33 from EUR35, Buy.

Hugo Boss beat 3Q26 sales by about 3% and EBIT by about 12%, but cut FY26 guidance. Sales are now expected to fall high-single-digits at constant FX, and EBIT guidance is EUR250-300m (from EUR300-350m). Retail fell 8% in 3Q and October showed no improvement. Citi cuts FY26E/27E/28E EBIT by about 9%/19%/14%. TP EUR38.5, Neutral. Frasers holds 49.4% of the stock.

European Oil & Gas Services: Brazil's CADE conditionally approved the Saipem-Subsea7 merger. The European Phase II decision is expected in early 2027. On 2028E EV/EBITDA the combined entity trades at about a 60% discount to TechnipFMC.

US auto sales for October were 1.34m units, up about 4% y/y (one more business day), with SAAR at 15.7m versus 16m in September. Inventory rose 120.3k units m/m to about 2.83m, and incentives rose $133 to $3,493 per car. STLA US sales fell about 9% y/y and its share fell to 7.2% from 8.1% in September.

European investment platforms: October trading rose 8% m/m at Avanza and fell 1% at both Nordnet and flatexDEGIRO. Annualised net flows of 5-6% at the Nordic platforms track below Q4 consensus. Citi rates Avanza and flatexDEGIRO Buy and Nordnet Neutral.
Global flights in Week 44 were -2.0% y/y (vs -2.1%). China was -5.6%, APAC ex-China -4.7%, Europe +2.1%, US +2.6% and the Middle East -16.8%.

Citi Global Macro Strategy expects equities to trade well into year end after the US midterms, since the median pullback is only 3-4% and has mostly occurred. It prefers European equities, which benefit more from lower oil and carry less data center build-out risk, and re-enters its EM FX carry basket as its vol warning indicator fell below its danger level.

The Riksbank hiked for the first time since 2023 and signalled more. Citi still expects only one more hike, in early 2027. Eurozone headline inflation reaches 4% while core stays in its recent range, and wage indicators for 2027 suggest services inflation can slow further.
Oil: the Democratic midterm win adds to US-Iran dealmaking momentum, and oil and gas sold off. Brent fell to $95/bbl and TTF to EUR85/MWh. Re-escalation risks remain in the near term.

Citi's gold base case (60% probability) is $4,500/oz on a 0-3 month view and $5,000/oz on 6-12 months if the Strait of Hormuz reopens and the Yemen/Saudi conflict de-escalates by year-end. The bear case (30%) sees $3,500/oz on a continued impasse, persistent inflation and rate hikes.

Citi FX Strategy says the post-midterm moves (lower yields, lower USD, higher equities) match the typical historical response, so it would be cautious about reading signal in them. It wants to fade post-midterm USD weakness, especially against EUR, and look to re-engage EURNOK downside at better levels.

earnings_insights: Rheinmetall pre-released Q3 headline numbers. FY26 guidance cut to sales of EUR13.2bn (previously EUR13.7-14.2bn) and a margin of 18.5% (previously 19%). These are company guidance figures.
Arm F2Q27 reported: sales beat by 5% and EPS by 8% (reported vs consensus, per Citi). Data Center royalties doubled y/y.
Novo Nordisk 3Q reported: adjusted sales and operating income guide points to roughly 3% FY26 consensus upgrades. Citi raised its own FY26 estimates 3-5%. Novo declined to commit to 2027 growth.
Ferrari Q3 26 reported: met earnings and EBIT margin expectations, with 22% specials delivery. FY26 EBIT guidance raised about 1%.

Flutter 3Q26 reported below Citi's estimates. FY26e revenue/adjusted EBITDA forecasts fall 2%/9% and adjusted EPS by 23% (Citi estimate changes). FY26 guidance was cut at the mid-point for both US and International.
Hugo Boss 3Q26 reported: sales beat by about 3% and EBIT by about 12% versus expectations. FY26 EBIT guidance cut to EUR250-300m from EUR300-350m. Retail was down 8% in 3Q26.

Zalando 3Q26 reported solid. Citi forecasts FY26e adjusted EBIT of EUR712m (forecast) against guidance of EUR680-720m. 3Q26 gross margin was worse than expected, with sneaker inventory clearance a roughly 65bps headwind (Citi estimate).

Schaeffler 3Q26 results confirmed further restructuring. Citi forecasts FY26-28e adjusted EBIT of EUR1,057m/EUR1,333m/EUR1,689m (forecasts) and FY28e margin targets of 6-8% were reiterated by management.
Stora Enso 3Q26 results reported. Management cited a mixed demand environment. Citi trims FY26e/27e EBIT slightly (forecast changes).
Technogym Q3 organic growth was about +3% ex-FX and the result was in line, per Citi.
Geberit 3Q was resilient and management signalled sequential moderation in volume growth into 4Q.
Wolters Kluwer trading update on 4 November reiterated FY26E margin guidance and guided restructuring charges higher.
Huhtamaki: FY26e EBIT broadly unchanged and FY27e EBIT cut about 7% (Citi estimate changes). FY26e includes a EUR23m one-off gain in Flexible Packaging.
Upcoming: DNB Capital Markets Day on 10 November. Nordea Danish AML investigation outcome due 9 November.

European gas fell alongside oil on renewed diplomacy.
Global flights look to be finding a plateau as Europe (+2.1%) and the US (+2.6%) offset Asia weakness.
